decisions.reason: As a two-component resin injection unit it builds directly on our established injection, pumping and plural-component know-how, so despite limited later website evidence we would more likely retain and refine it than withdraw it.

This product is also very close to our core application and fluid-handling capabilities, though overlap with other resin injection units raises some portfolio-rationalisation risk if demand proves too narrow.
An automatic airless spray gun fits squarely within our long-standing spray equipment knowledge base, service network and customer applications, making continued commercialization the likely choice.
A manual airless spray gun is highly aligned with our core product family and customer needs, so our absorptive capacity to improve and support it is strong and favors keeping it on the market.

An air-assisted airless spray gun remains closely related to our existing spray technology competencies and industrial customer base, so we would usually keep it unless sales were clearly disappointing.

The data logger is adjacent to our coating equipment business but relies more on digital and monitoring capabilities that are less central to our traditional strengths, and its reduced website prominence suggests weaker standalone traction.
